title: Dominic and the Will
premise: Estate lawyer Mirabel Villalobos is hired to read the will of Edmund Halloway, a reclusive clockmaker whose death certificate predates his own funeral. The will names a beneficiary who cannot be found — a man whose confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the burial, claiming he killed no one but knows who did. As Mirabel decodes a ledger hidden in the numbering of Halloway's clocks, he discovers the inheritance is not money but evidence: proof that Halloway faked his death to survive an old crime, and that someone in Mirabel's own firm helped bury it. In the end, Mirabel must choose between closing the case cleanly and exposing the truth, and he chooses truth — at the cost of his partnership, his reputation, and the safety he built his life on.
about_author: Yara Amberdale spent a decade as a probate clerk in coastal New England before turning to fiction, and her mysteries are known for their uncanny fidelity to the paperwork of death. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where she keeps her late grandmother's ledgers for inspiration.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Mirabel Villalobos, POV. A courier delivers a sealed will for Edmund Halloway — dated three days after his certified death. Mirabel's pride in never refusing a case wars with professional dread. Emotional beat: cold fascination masking unease.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Before the reading, an unsigned confession letter arrives: 'I killed no one, but I know who did.' The postmark is the day after Halloway's funeral. Beat: the hook tightens; Mirabel decides to attend the reading personally.

chapters.title: The Reading at Graywater House
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV, at the decaying Halloway estate. The will leaves everything to 'the man in the eleventh hour' — no name. The family bristles; the housekeeper flinches. Beat: theatrical mystery deepens into genuine menace.

chapters.title: Eleven Clocks, One Hour
chapters.summary: Mirabel examines Halloway's workshop: eleven clocks, all stopped at different times except one running fast. He suspects the 'eleventh hour' is literal. Beat: first thrill of the puzzle; a sense of being watched.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper Who Waited
chapters.summary: POV shift to Agnes Pell, the housekeeper, who reveals Halloway grew paranoid in his final year, burning papers and whispering about 'the ledger of what we survived.' Beat: grief entangled with guilt.

chapters.title: A Firm With Old Clients
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Back at his firm, senior partner Corliss Dane urges him to drop the case — oddly specific warnings. Mirabel notices Halloway's file bears a second, older reference number. Beat: suspicion turns inward.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Numbered
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. The stopped clocks' times correspond to page-and-line numbers in a standard estate ledger — pointing to transactions from 1974 under a shell company. Beat: breakthrough euphoria curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Man in the Eleventh Hour
chapters.summary: POV of Tobias Wren, the letter's author, hiding in a boarding house. He was Halloway's apprentice; the confession was dictated to him to mail after the funeral. Someone has been searching for him. Beat: hunted desperation.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Four
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV, digging archives: the shell company covered a fire at a mill that killed four people — officially accidental. Halloway was the night watchman who lived. Beat: the theme of survival's price surfaces.

chapters.title: Corliss Knows
chapters.summary: Mirabel confronts Dane gently; Dane deflects but slips a detail only an insider would know. Mirabel realizes his own firm handled the 1974 cover-up. Beat: betrayal, vertigo of lost trust.

chapters.title: Broken Glass in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Mirabel returns to Graywater House to find the eleventh clock smashed and Agnes unconscious on the floor. She survives but remembers nothing. Beat: the mystery turns violent; stakes become physical.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. He finally contacts Mirabel through a coded classified ad matching the ledger's cipher. He reveals Halloway didn't start the fire — he witnessed who did, and blackmailed silence to survive. Beat: reluctant alliance formed.

chapters.title: The Price of Witnessing
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Meeting Tobias in a rail yard, he hears the full account: the arsonist was a young Corliss Dane, protecting the firm's client. Halloway took hush money and forty years of fear. Beat: moral weight settles; anger hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Someone Closes the File
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. His office is searched; the original will vanishes from the firm safe. Dane offers him a partnership and a quiet exit. Beat: temptation offered plainly — the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Agnes Remembers
chapters.summary: Agnes, POV, recovering in hospital. She recalls a visitor the night Halloway died — a man with the firm's old brass tie pin — and that Halloway's death certificate was signed by a doctor who never came. Beat: memory as weapon; grief becomes testimony.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Following the ledger's final entry, he finds Halloway's true will hidden inside the running clock: it leaves everything to Tobias, contingent on public truth. Beat: the inheritance revealed — not wealth, but witness.

chapters.title: Deadline at Probate
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Dane moves to have the missing will declared void and the estate sealed, with a hearing in seventy-two hours. Mirabel realizes whoever controls the paper controls the past. Beat: ticking-clock pressure begins.

chapters.title: What Tobias Carried
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. Pursued, he retrieves the last piece: Halloway's recorded deposition naming Dane, entrusted to him decades ago. He nearly burns it out of terror, then doesn't. Beat: the cost of courage paid by the least protected.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. In probate court, Dane produces a forged revocation. Mirabel enters the ledger, the deposition, and Agnes's testimony, dismantling the forgery line by line. Beat: climax of intellect — the lawyer's craft turned to reckoning.

chapters.title: Confession, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax. Tobias takes the stand and reads Halloway's confession letter in full. Dane unravels; charges are referred. Mirabel wins the case he can't close quietly — and loses the firm. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Weeks later: disbarment proceedings loom, but Tobias receives the estate and offers Mirabel work as counsel to a foundation funding fire-safety reform. Beat: bittersweet renewal; the price accepted.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Clock
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV, coda. At Graywater House, now restored, he winds a new twelfth clock set to the present hour and mails his resignation letter. Some inheritances are debts you choose to pay. Beat: quiet resolution, forward-looking peace.
